content:
arjun: heads-up — spun up a quick prototype for adaptive telemetry filtering by route + SLA tier. thinking head+tail mix: keep first few spans of each trace, tail-sample errors, and bump rates for higher-tier customers. want feedback before I wire this into otel-collector.

minji: nice. can you sketch the policy? interested in how we avoid high-cardinality explosion for routes like /status or /health.

arjun: short sketch:
```
processors:
  routesampler:
    type: route_based
    default_rate: 0.02
    route_overrides:
      /generate: 0.2
      /embed: 0.05
    tier_overrides:
      gold: 0.5
      silver: 0.1
    head_spans: 3
    tail_errors: true
```
idea is to: 1) always keep first 3 spans (head) so traces have context, 2) for error traces keep full tail, 3) per-route base rates and per-customer tier boosts. for noisy routes we'll set very low default.

gabe: two quick concerns: 1) how do we define "error" consistently across services (http 5xx vs span.status)? 2) can we enforce per-customer quotas so sampling doesn't let a gold tenant blow storage?

arjun: good q. plan is to treat span.status=ERROR || http.status>=500 as tail triggers. also add a per-tenant ingestion cap: if a tenant exceeds X spans/day post-sampling, throttle sampling rate downward and surface in console.

olivia: UX ask — we need console primitives: show sampled vs ingested counts, projected storage, and a preview when you change a route rule. otherwise product teams will be scared to touch rates. :eyes:

priya: +1 on console preview. also we should surface bias metrics: are we over/under-sampling specific user cohorts? maybe show distribution by customer_tier and route.

minji: storage math pls. if default_rate=0.02 and head_spans=3, some high-traffic routes will still generate lots of head spans. maybe we only head-sample once per request_id, not per span. also dedupe health checks.

arjun: yep request_id dedupe to avoid repeated head spans. health/status route explicit blacklist: sample 0.001 and drop headers that increase cardinality (user-agent etc) for those routes.

gabe: how about exporters? we need partitioned downstream flows: high-fidelity traces -> long-retention hot index (for gold/debug), sampled set -> analytics store (BQ), and minimal metadata -> metrics pipeline. also ensure OTLP exporter tags original_sampling_decision so we can recalc if needed.

arjun: plan is two exporters: full-trace-exporter (only for tail/error and gold overrides) with 90d retention, and sampled-exporter with 30d retention. will add attribute otel.sampling.reason and otel.sampling.policy to spans.

telemetry-bot: otelcol: routesampler applied to 8 services, sampling rate summary: default=2%, /generate=20%, /embed=5%, gold_override=50% (prototype run)

olivia: rollout plan? small canary per region, expose feature flag to toggle per-tenant rules. need UX for canary -> ramp -> global.

priya: add evals: daily regression tests comparing error detection recall on sampled vs full-trace baseline. want alarms if recall drops >5%.

minji: agree. also add a debug-mode passthrough where we capture full traces for a random 0.1% of requests for stats and estimator calibration.

arjun: action items:
- I'll push prototype config to staging otel collector and enable for 5 services (arjun)
- olivia to spec console preview and quota UI (olivia)
- priya to write recall/regression tests (priya)
- gabe to sketch exporter retention tiers and quota enforcement (gabe)

arjun: ok i'll post the PR once collector config is tidy. thanks all :thumbsup:
